title: The 9-Bar Thermofluidic Engine
subtitle: Why espresso machines don't melt, stall, or drift: The coupled thermodynamics and hydraulic dynamics behind sub-minute thermal equilibrium and non-pulsatile 9-bar extraction.

channeling.definition: The formation of low-resistance fissures or erosion cracks through a packed bed, allowing pressurized fluid to bypass the surrounding matrix and create uneven extraction.

permeability.definition: A measure of the ability of a porous material to transmit fluids under an applied pressure gradient, governed by void size, particle geometry, and bed compaction.

thermal-conductivity.definition: The intrinsic material property quantifying its ability to conduct heat energy across a temperature gradient, typically measured in Watts per meter-Kelvin (W/m·K).

no-slip-condition.definition: A fundamental boundary condition in fluid mechanics stating that at a solid boundary, fluid molecules have zero velocity relative to the solid surface, forming a boundary layer.

dean-vortices.definition: Pairs of counter-rotating secondary fluid currents formed in curved pipes, driven by centrifugal imbalances between the fast-moving fluid core and the slower boundary layers.

pid-controller.definition: A standard three-term feedback loop algorithm that calculates an error between a desired setpoint and measured value, applying proportional, integral, and derivative corrections.

triac.definition: A solid-state bidirectional AC semiconductor switch that controls power to heating elements and motors by rapidly turning on and off at specific points in the AC sine wave.

epdm.definition: Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer; a durable synthetic elastomer widely used for high-temperature water and steam gaskets due to its outstanding resistance to heat and compression set.

fkm.definition: Fluoroelastomer (commonly known as Viton); a premium rubber material engineered for high chemical and thermal stability, commonly used in solenoid valve seals.
